Senses.Explanation: The recurring line says that what falls with a thud is no other thing; some cases stage it by dropping a staff or whisk, while Gulin preserves it metrically. Gulin preserves the recurring line in verse, Zhenjing drops the staff and asks what the thing is, Xiaoshan repeats the pair after throwing down the whisk, and Feiyin does so with the staff.

Senses.Explanation: A round sitting mat is the portable mat on which a person sits in the hall or quarters. Chan records place bodies on the mat, speak of wearing one through long use, carry it, break it, or cite it in encounters. These are uses of monastery furniture; the mat remains concrete rather than becoming the name of a procedure.
